articles.title: Combing-triggered electrostimulation synchronizing deep delivery for rapid hair regrowth in androgenetic alopecia
GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root
articles.abstract: Abstract Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

articles.title: Strategically tuning oxygen in multiple phases for high-performance titanium alloys
Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
Fire risk to U.S. structures nearly triples by mid-century
Ca2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots
Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins
articles.abstract: Abstract An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBV p ) in healthy adults ( n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBV p ) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ 40&42 , GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses.

articles.title: Copper-modified nickel membrane reactor for electrochemical hydrogenation in low-conductivity water
Relaxase asymmetry drives initiation of bacterial conjugation
articles.abstract: Abstract Bacterial conjugation drives horizontal gene transfer and accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance. In F-plasmid systems, the bifunctional relaxase-helicase TraI initiates transfer by nicking plasmid DNA through its trans-esterase activity and subsequently unwinding the plasmid via its helicase domains. Previous evidence suggested that two TraI molecules act cooperatively, yet how their activities are spatially and temporally coordinated has remained unclear. Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of a functionally asymmetric TraI homodimer and show that dimerisation is mediated predominantly by single-stranded DNA. Trans-esterasedriven duplex melting at the origin of transfer by one TraI molecule enables helicase loading by a second TraI molecule onto the transfer strand of the intact plasmid. Although the trans-esterase domain is intrinsically active, the host factor IHF inhibits nicking until helicase loading occurs. These findings uncover a regulatory loop coupling strand nicking with helicase engagement, defining a unified mechanism for initiating conjugative DNA processing.

articles.title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
articles.abstract: Abstract Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella . Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

articles.title: Neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
articles.abstract: Abstract Schizophrenia spectrum disorders have substantial genetic liability, but their stable incidence and clinical heterogeneity leave open contributions from non-genetic mechanisms. Though autoimmune encephalitis demonstrates that anti-neural antibodies can cause psychosis, encephalitis antibodies are uncommon in schizophrenia. Here we show that multi-platform autoantigen profiling of cerebrospinal fluid and plasma detects rare, anti-neural autoantibodies in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. By antibody profiling the cerebrospinal fluid of 32 schizophrenia spectrum participants and 32 neuropsychiatrically unaffected controls by brain tissue immunostaining, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry, phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing, and plasma by complementary protein microarrays, we identify three autoantibodies, including to alpha-crystallin B. The anti-alpha-crystallin B antibody preferentially recognizes phosphorylated serine-45 and is absent from the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with untreated multiple sclerosis, a disease with frequent antibodies to unphosphorylated alpha-crystallin B. These findings do not define autoimmune psychosis as a new disease but support broader autoantibody searches in psychotic disorders.

articles.title: Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
High-performance annealing-free wurtzite ferroelectric field-effect transistors with ultrathin oxide semiconductors for neuromorphic computing
The CCCH-type zinc-finger PfMD3 promotes translation for malaria parasite transmission
articles.abstract: Abstract Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 ( Pf MD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of Pf MD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of Pf MD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these Pf MD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in Pf MD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that Pf MD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, Pf MD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes Pf MD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility.

articles.title: Hexafluoroethane purification via molecular sieving in a molecule-trap metal-organic framework
Hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis prevents pro-metastatic niche formation through metabolic rewiring of inflammatory monocytes
articles.abstract: Abstract Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α–XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte–IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

articles.title: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
articles.abstract: Abstract Neuromuscular compartments provide the functional substrate for finger-specific motor control, yet their in vivo three-dimensional (3D) architecture remains unresolved because of the absence of clear fascial landmarks for imaging. Here, we present a multimodal imaging framework combining ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide volumetric compartment segmentation and in vivo architectural reconstruction of the flexor digitorum superficialis. During isolated finger flexion, tissue movement directions estimated from dynamic ultrasound delineate compartment contours, which are mapped into a 3D MRI reference to generate volumetric compartment masks. Using these masks as constraints, tractography reconstructs 3D fiber trajectories and yields compartment-specific architectural measurements. In ten healthy individuals, compartment topology and fiber orientations were consistent with classic cadaveric anatomy, and estimated compartments accurately predicted surface electromyography amplitude distributions. This framework provides 3D fiber trajectories and quantitative parameters for finger-specific computational models, establishing a foundation for subject-specific neuromuscular digital twins and next-generation neuromuscular interfaces.

articles.title: Substantial Neotropical bat diversity likely remains undescribed and vulnerable to extinction
articles.abstract: Abstract Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. Here, we integrate molecular species delimitation, phylogenetic inference, ecological niche modelling, and spatial conservation analyses to identify 95 Neotropical bat lineages that may represent undescribed species within 45 complexes, revealing that at least one-fifth of the recognized taxa may harbor hidden diversity spanning the entire evolutionary spectrum. This overlooked diversity faces a countdown to extinction: 62% of complexes face imminent habitat loss, and most are projected to lose over 50% of their suitable habitat by 2070. At current description rates, formally recognizing this diversity would take decades, a timeframe these putative species cannot afford. We develop a Hidden Species Richness (HSR) Index that pinpoints ten hidden diversity hotspots where undescribed richness coincides with significant human threats and extreme climate vulnerability. These hotspots highlight regions where research efforts are most needed, transforming crises into priorities. This race against extinction requires immediate taxonomic attention to document this biodiversity before it vanishes.

articles.title: Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS

Global Steel Decarbonization
under Policy, Technology,
and Resource Constraints: A Process-Unit Agent-Based Model
articles.abstract: Abstract Deep decarbonization of steel requires low-emission technologies to be deployed through a long-lived and heterogeneous asset fleet without disrupting steel supply. We developed a country-resolved agent-based model that follows global steel process units annually from 2023 to 2060. Units choose among continued operation, renewal, retrofit, conversion, retirement, and new construction, subject to construction time, linked upstream capacity, national production pathways, and annual supplies of scrap, hydrogen, natural gas, and pellets. Four scenarios distinguish stronger climate policy from improved technology and resource availability. Global process-chain CO2 emissions decline by 67–79% by 2060, reaching 0.476–0.737 Gt. The integrated case achieves the lowest emissions, but the two-component interventions do not independently outperform the reference case. Stronger policy changes when assets enter a finite transition queue, whereas technology and material conditions determine whether replacement routes can be built and operated at that time. By 2060, Scrap-EAF supplies 74–80% of crude steel, but residual unabated blast furnaces and coal-based direct reduction keep national steel pathways above their allocated levels in many countries. Deep decarbonization, therefore, depends on coordinating asset turnover, construction, and complementary material systems, rather than on technology availability or carbon-price pressure alone.

articles.title:
Mechanistic
Insights
into Humic Acid-Mediated Photosensitized
Activation of Mn(VII) under UVA Irradiation
articles.abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet A/permanganate [UVA/Mn(VII)] is a promising advanced oxidation process (AOP), while few studies have noticed that humic acid (HA) could enhance microcontaminant degradation in the process. For the first time, the promotive effect of HA and the underlying mechanisms were investigated in UVA/Mn(VII). HA significantly enhanced the generation of hydroxyl radical (HO•) and reactive manganese species (RMnS). Consequently, the pseudo-first-order reaction rate constants for microcontaminant degradation in UVA/Mn(VII)/HA were several to tens of times those in UVA/Mn(VII). The promotive effect of HA was attributed to the enhanced Mn(VII) activation by photogenerated reactive intermediates derived from irradiated HA. Among them, the excited triplet state of HA (3HA*) played a major role, which was also supported by benzophenone (BP), a model triplet state photosensitizer. The second-order reaction rate constants of Mn(VII) with 3HA* and 3BP* were determined to be 2.54(±0.31) × 108 and 2.88(±0.10) × 109 M–1 s–1, respectively. Spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations supported an electron transfer mechanism for the reactions of Mn(VII) with 3HA* and 3BP*. Mn(VII) accepted one electron from 3HA*/3BP* and was reduced to Mn(VI), which underwent disproportionation to form Mn(VII) and Mn(V), followed by HO• and other RMnS generation. These findings provide novel perspectives for the application of UVA/Mn(VII) in practical water treatment.

articles.title: Issue Publication Information

Recovering Rare
Earth Elements from Mining Effluent
via Synergistic Angstrom-Scale Confinement and Phosphate-Mediated
Coordination in MXene Membranes
articles.abstract: Abstract Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from complex aqueous streams is essential for advancing sustainable resource recovery but remains hindered by low REE concentrations and strong competition with impurity ions. Herein, we introduce a biomimetic MXene membrane that integrates phosphate-based molecular recognition with angstrom-level control of interlayer spacing to achieve the selective and continuous recovery of REEs from wastewaters. By intercalating aminophosphonic molecules within Ti3C2Tx layers, the membrane precisely tunes the nanochannel size and establishes coordinatively active oxygen sites that preferentially bind trivalent lanthanides under nanoconfinement. Such a design enables a synergistic mechanism in which steric exclusion and ligand–metal coordination coregulate ion transport, leading to markedly improved selectivity toward REE recovery. The optimized 2-AEP-M membrane exhibited a Ca2+/Dy3+ selectivity of 243.47 in simulated solutions and 130.69 in actual REE mining wastewater. After membrane separation and subsequent precipitation and calcination, REEs constituted 90.2% of the quantified cationic species in the recovered solid products. Experimental and computational analyses reveal that phosphate groups promote Dy3+ coordination, underpinning the observed ion discrimination. The membrane also demonstrates antiswelling stability and antibacterial properties, supporting its potential for long-term deployment. This work integrates chemical affinity with angstrom-confined transport, offering a platform for precise ion separation and sustainable REE recovery.

articles.title:
Targeted
Coupling
of Electrogenerated Reactive Oxygen
Species for Deep Pollutant Mineralization
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment. However, the inherent limitations of single-component reactive oxygen species (ROS) and their low yield impede thorough mineralization of organic pollutants and elevate energy consumption. Herein, we develop a directed ROS coupling oxidation (DRCO) system, which employs a Ni–Sb–SnO2 anode that leverages Ni(III)/Ni(II) redox cycling for highly selective OH generation, coupled with a CrMn@C anode for 1O2 production, significantly enhancing the coexisting ROS yield. By leveraging the electron-withdrawing and donating synergistic effect of •OH and 1O2, the DRCO system removes 61.2–78.5% total organic carbon (TOC) for diverse organics within 20 min. The observed kinetic constants are 1.4–52.6 times higher than those of systems that use •OH or 1O2 alone. Furthermore, the DRCO system achieves 85.4% TOC removal for actual pharmaceutical wastewater and sustains operational stability over a 120 h continuous flow period. Compared to commercial anodes, the DRCO system reduces energy consumption by 72% (to 12.02 kW·h·kgTOC–1) while effectively suppressing the accumulation of toxic intermediate products. This work demonstrates that high-selectivity •OH generation and the elucidated dual-ROS synergistic mechanism jointly offer a viable strategy toward efficient and energy-conscious electrochemical water purification.

articles.title: Issue Editorial Masthead

Biogeochemical
Control Points for Mitigating Metal(loid)
Risk in Rice under Global Change
articles.abstract: Abstract The uptake of arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), and mercury (Hg) in rice is a global health concern. The variable biogeochemical processes that govern contamination risk, along with increased anthropogenic pressures, present significant obstacles to implementing mitigation strategies. This perspective highlights the biogeochemical processes governing the mobility and rice uptake of metal(loid)s across the soil-rice continuum and provides recent insights into mitigation strategies. An overview of anthropogenic stressors that may further exacerbate rice contamination, particularly climate change, is also provided. Finally, in the context of historical knowledge, we identify and discuss a future roadmap for research priorities and mitigation strategies, including (1) addressing variability in soil-rice systems that alters metal(loid) uptake dynamics, (2) investigating practical applications and mitigation strategies for farmers, and (3) expanding research into the myriad effects climate change may have on metal(loid) cycling.

articles.title:
Climate-Driven
Sink-to-Source
Transitions for Microplastics
in Terrestrial Systems
articles.abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as pervasive contaminants in terrestrial environments, where soils act as major dynamic reservoirs that retain particles but can also release them through hydrological, erosional, and atmospheric pathways. Climate change is altering the physical, hydrological, and biogeochemical controls that govern the MP retention-release balance. This review develops a climate-driven sink-to-source transition framework in which terrestrial systems shift episodically from retention-dominated to export-active states. We synthesize evidence that changes in freeze–thaw regimes and drought-rewetting reorganize pore networks and preferential flow; extreme rainfall and runoff can exceed hydrological retention and redistribute MPs vertically and laterally; and warming and salinization reconfigure interfacial interactions, polymer aging, aggregation behavior, and microbially mediated transport processes. Atmospheric entrainment and snowpack-snowmelt pathways further connect terrestrial MP reservoirs with other environmental compartments. Across these climate drivers, MP mobility depends on the coupled evolution of pore architecture, water flux, particle properties, and biogeochemical conditions rather than on any single forcing factor. By integrating laboratory studies, field observations, and emerging modeling perspectives, this review provides a mechanistic foundation for predicting terrestrial MP redistribution and associated environmental risks under ongoing climate change.

articles.title:
Constructing Prospective
Multiregional Input-Output
Tables via Scenario-Constrained Optimization for Future Environmental
Footprint Assessment
articles.abstract: Abstract Prospective multiregional input-output (MRIO) tables that integrate scenarios from integrated assessment models (IAMs) support forward-looking environmental footprint analysis, but the trade-off between historical structural fidelity and scenario compliance has not been quantified. We constructed 12 prospective MRIO tables from EXIOBASE 2019 and the IMAGE SSP2 scenario for 2035, including a Leontief-based projection and 11 optimization-based projections under different combinations of scenario constraints on GDP, value added, sector outputs, as well as energy and agriculture consumption. Among the constraints, those on energy and agriculture consumption were satisfied at the highest cost in coefficient deviations from the Leontief-based projection and shifted the corresponding transaction flows most significantly. Regional shares of the global carbon footprint remained stable, but sectoral attribution within each region was substantially reshuffled, and the identification of high-growth consumption hotspots was sensitive to scenario compliance level. Some hotspots persisted at all levels of compliance. The consumption-based carbon footprint driven by China’s final energy demand grew the fastest and emerged as a major new hotspot in 2035. The footprint of livestock consumption showed persistent high growth in multiple regions and India and the Rest of Asia rose in environmental significance through their industrial sectors.

articles.title:
Why
Phytate Persists: Mechanisms of Exceptional Binding
and Stability on Soil Mineral Surfaces
articles.abstract: Abstract Phytate, a six-phosphate compound that stores plant phosphorus, is a stable component of soil phosphorus, yet mechanisms underlying its persistence remain unclear. Here, we combined adsorption experiments, spectroscopy, X-ray scattering, and molecular modeling to investigate phytate interactions with five soil minerals: goethite, hematite, quartz, montmorillonite, and kaolinite. Iron oxides exhibited up to 5-fold greater adsorption capacities than quartz and clays. Natural organic matter caused negligible desorption of mineral-bound phytate, whereas phytate displaced adsorbed natural organic matter, demonstrating competitive and stable phytate-mineral associations. Adsorption capacities normalized to orthophosphate binding-site densities implied multiphosphate coordination for phytate on iron oxides, but binding beyond nominal orthophosphate sites on montmorillonite. Molecular dynamics simulations captured one to three phosphate groups in phytate associations with iron oxides; metal cation screening of electrostatic repulsion facilitated binding on negatively charged quartz and montmorillonite. Infrared spectroscopy revealed coupled vibrational responses of phosphate and inositol ring moieties on goethite, but primarily phosphate responses on montmorillonite. X-ray total scattering determined a feature at 2.7 Å, supporting inner-sphere coordination on iron oxides and consistent with quantum mechanics-based energy calculations, whereas quartz and clay features indicated interfacial reorganization. These findings establish mineral-specific mechanisms of phytate stabilization, with implications for persistence and bioavailability in soils.

articles.title: Community of Practice

Hydrophilic Nanoisland
Interface Engineering for Conquering
Activity–Stability Trade-Off in High-Efficiency Salt Lake Lithium
Extraction
articles.abstract: Abstract The adsorption-based lithium extraction technology from ultralow-grade salt lake brine is severely restricted by the inherent activity–stability trade-off of traditional granular Li/Al-LDHs adsorbents (GLDHs). Herein, a nanoisland encapsulation strategy integrated with hydrophilic interface engineering is developed to fabricate Li/Al-LDHs composite granules with tailored hydrophilic interfaces (HILDHs), breaking the long-standing bottleneck of conventional aluminum-based lithium adsorbents used in the salt lake industry. Systematic experiments and multiscale simulations reveal that the strong water affinity of polyacrylonitrile cyano groups (−C≡N) creates a highly hydrated microenvironment for rapid Li+ transport, while the nanoisland-confined structure anchors Li/Al-LDHs nanosheets to preserve the layered framework under harsh deep desorption conditions, thus enabling excellent cycling stability. The optimized HILDHs deliver a 3.02-fold higher working adsorption capacity (7.25 mg g–1 vs 2.40 mg g–1 for GLDHs) in actual Qarhan old brine within 60 min, along with a 13.36-fold increase in adsorption rate constant, 40% lower rinsing water consumption, and excellent cycle stability. It is calculated the nanoisland encapsulation strategy can achieve a nearly 5-fold increase for the annual Li2CO3 production capacity from salt lake lithium industrial lines.

articles.title:
Modeling Decadal
Organosulfates in Particulate Matter
to Improve Estimations of Aerosol Hygroscopicity in the United States
articles.abstract: Abstract Organosulfates (OSs) can comprise a substantial fraction of secondary organic aerosol and exhibit significantly different hygroscopicity than inorganic sulfates, yet their spatiotemporal prevalence and climatic impacts remain poorly constrained because speciated measurements are sparse and common chemical transport models do not explicitly represent OS formation. This study develops a flexible and robust modeling framework to quantify isoprene-derived OS (iOS) concentrations and OS impacts on aerosol hygroscopicity (κ) across the contiguous United States (U.S.) for summers spanning 2013–2022. Using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model with updated iOS chemistry, simulations reproduce Interagency Monitoring of Protected Visual Environments (IMPROVE) network-derived organosulfur and inorganic sulfate and agree with speciated iOS measurements from filter analyses. OS concentrations are elevated in the eastern U.S., with summertime mean values up to 0.51 μg m–3. OS formation produces a net 5.6% decrease in κ (direct OS contribution, +2.8%; indirect, −8.4% via sulfate reduction). We apply an interpretable machine-learning surrogate to identify predictive features associated with OS variability and enable efficient estimation without rerunning CMAQ. These results provide the first observation-validated, high-spatial-coverage OS reconstruction and nationwide quantification of OS-driven κ changes, underscoring the importance of representing OS formation and expanded observations to improve aerosol-cloud radiative effect assessments.

articles.title:
Context-Aware
Multitask Learning for Aquatic and Soil
Ecotoxicity Prediction from Fragmented ECOTOX Records
articles.abstract: Abstract Large ecotoxicity databases contain extensive evidence, yet heterogeneous reporting and sparse coverage across chemicals, species, end points, and conditions limit predictive use. From relational U.S. EPA ECOTOX, we linked 1,234,077 traceable records and constructed model-ready aquatic and soil data sets of 219,818 and 11,532 records. We developed a context-aware multitask model that preserves end point-specific responses while sharing information across molecular, biological, and experimental contexts. On held-out condition keys and parent-species-task combinations, four-seed ensembles achieved pooled R2 of 0.758/0.751 for aquatic toxicity and 0.628/0.537 for soil toxicity. Compared with same-input single-task models, multitask fitting reduced soil task-macro mean absolute error (MAE) by 0.136/0.156 across 16 task heads; aquatic point estimates also favored sharing, although uncertainty across all aquatic task heads was not estimable. Under canonical-parent holdout, frozen shared representations reduced task-macro MAE by 0.170–0.180 in aquatic and 0.093–0.125 in soil tree models versus molecular-only inputs, indicating reusable predictive information. Multidimensional training support stratified parent-holdout errors, meeting prespecified criteria fully for soil and partially for aquatic predictions; benefits weakened under stronger structural separation. These results show model-ready ECOTOX data can support context-aware toxicity prediction across a sparse experimental matrix, helping prioritize informative measurements and providing a predictive evidence base for environmental hazard assessment.

articles.title:
Coupled
Geophysical
and Technoeconomic Industrial
Growth Constraints on Geological Carbon Storage Scale-Up: Application
to UK Offshore Resources
articles.abstract: Abstract Geological carbon dioxide storage is central to meeting many national climate change commitments, but large-scale deployment may be limited by both techno-economic rates of growth and physics-based processes imposed by subsurface geology. We develop a modeling framework for the assessment of feasible CO2 storage scale-up trajectories that unifies constraints arising from industrial rates of growth, dynamic injection rate limits from reservoir pressurization, and static maximum cumulative storage resource. We employ logistic and Gompertz models to represent policy-compliant deployment trajectories, parametrized by the total cumulative storage resource. We then use a simplified physics model to estimate the resulting regional subsurface pressurization along these trajectories. Growth curves where reservoir pressurization exceeds safe limits are updated by reducing the static storage resource until residing in the safe deployment range. The result is both a growth trajectory and static storage resource achievable subject to injectivity limits. Applying the framework to the United Kingdom (UK), we find that offshore storage resources are sufficient to accommodate all government midcentury deployment rate scenarios up to 175 Mt yr–1. Cumulative storage of up to 78 Gt, representing a reference estimate of the UK storage resource base used in national planning, can be achieved under Gompertz growth trajectories. The more aggressive logistic trajectories are constrained by reservoir pressure, limiting the achievable resource base to 69 Gt. The framework is transferable to other regions to assess the feasibility of policy-driven CO2 storage pathways under coupled industrial growth and geophysical constraints, informing national decarbonization planning and global integrated assessment models.

articles.title:
Highly Selective
Lithium Extraction from Shale Gas
Wastewater Using Al- and F-Doped LiMn2O4 Electrode in Rocking-Chair Capacitive Deionization
articles.abstract: Abstract Selective lithium extraction from shale gas wastewater (SGW) offers a promising strategy to expand lithium supply while reducing wastewater-management burdens. However, low Li+ concentrations and overwhelming competition from Na+ and Mg2+ make selective and energy-efficient extraction challenging. Lithium manganese oxide (LMO) is attractive for electrochemical Li extraction but remains limited by insufficient cycling stability and selectivity in complex ionic matrices. Here, we investigate the effects of Al and F modification of LMO on lithium extraction in a rocking-chair capacitive deionization system. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations show that the optimized modification contracts the spinel lattice and produces near-surface enrichment of F-containing species, improving electrochemical reversibility. Electrochemical analyses and density functional theory calculations further indicate favorable Li+ transport and stronger migration restrictions for Na+ and Mg2+ after lattice entry. In a simulated SGW matrix with a Li/Na/Mg molar ratio of 1:100:1, LMO-Al-F achieves a Li adsorption capacity of 9.54 mg g–1, Li/Na and Li/Mg separation factors of 2216 and 1509, and an energy consumption of 4.21 Wh mol–1 Li. Strong Li selectivity is also maintained in real SGW. After 100 competitive-ion cycles, 78% of adsorption capacity is retained, supporting repeated Li-selective extraction under high-salinity conditions.

articles.title:
Water Footprint
and Scarcity Risks of Low-Carbon Fuels
articles.abstract: Abstract Production of ammonia, methanol, and hydrogen is key to decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors but is also water-intensive. However, the water implications of scaling these energy carriers under low-carbon pathways remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate direct water consumption with facility-level geospatial analysis and hydrological modeling to quantify water-scarcity exposure across each production facility in North America. Low-carbon production routes require more direct and indirect water consumption than conventional pathways, with electrolytic hydrogen and e-methanol increasing water-intensity by up to 5-fold in regions with limited renewable availability─a trade-off further amplified by supply chain effects, particularly for solar PV-based electricity and direct air capture-based CO2 feedstocks. Water scarcity already affects about 58% of methanol production in Mexico, 2% of ammonia production in the U.S., and 5% and 27% of refinery production in the U.S. and Mexico, respectively. Under midcentury climate scenarios, exposure increases in both magnitude and spatial extent. Although irrigation accounts for over 80% of local water consumption in various fuel production facilities, municipalities and manufacturing often exert the greatest pressure on low-carbon fuel production, depending on the product and country.. These results demonstrate that technology choice, system design, and facility siting are as important as hydrology considerations in determining water risks. Incorporating water availability in low-carbon fuel projects is therefore essential to ensure that decarbonization pathways are scalable, operationally resilient, and truly sustainable.

articles.title:
Molecular Insights
into a Precursor–Chlorine
Trade-Off Governing Divergent Formation Pathways of PCDD/Fs and Emerging
Cl-PAHs in Waste Cocombustion of Cellulose, PET, and PVC
articles.abstract: Abstract Co-combustion of industrial and municipal solid waste (ISW/MSW) is widely practiced, yet PCDD/Fs and emerging chlorinated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (Cl-PAHs) formation under mixed-feedstock conditions remains poorly understood. Here, cellulose, polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) were combusted individually and cocombusted with MSW to elucidate how feedstock chemistry regulates chlorinated pollutant formation. Comprehensive mass-spectrometric profiling of target pollutants, aromatic precursors, and the top 50 combustion intermediates, combined with DFT calculations, revealed a precursor–chlorine trade-off governing pollutant formation. PET preferentially generated oxygenated aromatic intermediates, particularly dibenzofuran; PVC supplied the most PAHs and reactive chlorine, and cellulose primarily contributed carbon skeletons. Accordingly, two distinct pathways were proposed: dibenzofuran-centered, chlorination-limited formation of PCDD/Fs and stepwise aromatic growth followed by site-selective chlorination of Cl-PAHs. The higher HOMO energies of two representative PAHs, anthracene and phenanthrene, relative to dibenzofuran indicated their greater susceptibility to electrophilic chlorination. Consequently, Cl-PAHs exceeded PCDD/Fs by 1–3 orders of magnitude and accounted for 83.4% of estimated TEQ. Increasing chlorine availability alleviated the kinetic constraint on dibenzofuran chlorination, causing an approximately 42-fold increase in PCDD/F emissions at 20% PVC blending. These findings establish a molecular basis for feedstock-chemistry-guided management and broaden emission-control priorities from regulated PCDD/Fs to emerging Cl-PAHs.

articles.title:
Polyethylene Terephthalate
Oligomers in Disposable
Diapers: Occurrence, Dermal Exposure and Health Assessment
articles.abstract: Abstract Disposable infant diapers commonly use multicomponent nonwoven fabrics containing polyethylene terephthalate (PET), from which PET oligomer byproducts may be released and transferred to infant skin. In this study, 6 cyclic PET oligomers (C[TPA+EG]2–7) were detected in the top sheets and absorbent cores of 37 disposable diapers. ∑C[TPA+EG]2–7 averaged 198 ± 98.7 μg/g (top sheets) and 66.6 ± 49.2 μg/g (absorbent cores), dominated by C[TPA+EG]3 (95.9% and 92.3%). Oligomer levels positively correlated with diaper PET content, confirming an in situ polymer source. During a 3-day in-use study, 1348–2318 ng of oligomers migrated to infant buttock skin and remained partially after water washing, corresponding to an estimated C[TPA+EG]3 exposure of 8.80–182 ng/kg BW/day. Network toxicology and molecular docking identified potential targets and pathways associated with local skin effects, including inflammation, barrier regulation, apoptosis, and extracellular matrix remodeling, suggesting potential local skin-health implications. Our results establish diaper dermal contact as a critical infant plastic oligomer exposure route and raise health concerns for vulnerable infant skin.

articles.title:
Atmospheric Aging
Modifies the Toxicological Profile
of Biomass Burning Particles in Epithelial Lung Cells
articles.abstract: Abstract Wildfire activity and associated smoke emissions are increasing globally, leading to widespread exposure to biomass burning particulate matter (PM). Although people are mainly exposed to aged wildfire smoke rather than fresh emissions, the effects of atmospheric aging on wildfire particulate toxicity remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how atmospheric processing (“aging”) modifies biological effects of biomass burning particles (BBPs) generated under controlled flaming and smoldering combustion conditions. BB emissions were produced in the Photochemical Large Aerosol Chamber (PHOTO-LAC) and aged under alternating photochemical and dark conditions. Fresh and aged BBP extracts were subsequently sampled and tested in human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B). We assessed cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, oxidative DNA damage, genome-wide transcriptional responses, and inflammatory and extracellular matrix-related protein expression. Atmospheric aging substantially altered BBP toxicity in a combustion-dependent manner. Aged BBP enhanced intracellular reactive oxygen species formation and oxidative DNA damage, particularly for smoldering emissions, while cytotoxicity remained largely unchanged. In contrast, inflammatory and matrix-remodeling responses were attenuated with aging in smoldering particles but remained stable for flaming BBP. These findings demonstrate that atmospheric aging can simultaneously amplify oxidative and genotoxic stress while dampening inflammatory signaling, underscoring the need to incorporate aging state into health risk assessments of wildfire smoke exposure.
